Hey, Frank, it's Arthur. Look, I need to talk to you about that invention of yours, the one you've been working on. I've heard the rumors, and I'm hoping to God it's real, because here's the deal.

This theater, it's on the verge of collapse, and I'm not sure how much longer I can keep it running. The manager's been hiding financials from me, running up debt, pretending everything's fine. But I found out, and it's bad, real bad.

This invention of yours, the one you've been so confident about, it's gotta work. There's no maybe here. Mo, we'll see what happens. If this thing can really revolutionize the projection industry, then it's our last shot.

If it doesn't work, we're done. This place will fail, and I'll lose everything I built here. And frankly, so will you. We're in the same boat now.

I'm putting all my faith in you and that machine of yours. The entire future of this theater is riding on it.

The budget's tight, and I'm not sure how much more I can hide from the creditors. You understand what that means, don't you?
  We need something new, something to get people back in those seats. Something that makes them say, this is where I want to be.

So I need you to call me, and I need you to call me soon. Let me know where we stand. If this invention of yours is what you say it is, then we've got a chance. But if it's not, well, we'll be having a very different conversation. And I don't want it to come to that.
  I'm counting on you. I really am. Call me back and let's figure this out. This could be our last shot at turning this thing around. Please, don't let me down, Frank.

(Phone voice) Last, message. Thursday, June 29, 1995 at 7:27 a.m.

Hi, Frank. This is Dr. Jameson Kim from the Theoretical Physics Division at Cormack University. I hope I'm not interrupting.
  I imagine you're swamped with preparations for the big show at Atlas 9 this Friday. The advertisements have really built up anticipation for it.

I wanted to share something unusual we observed last week.

Around midnight for about a minute or so, my team recorded a highly concentrated energy signature, directly centered on the theater. It was a massive spike, unlike anything we've measured before, and then it disappeared just as quickly as it appeared. The rapid onset and dissipation are particularly intriguing.
  I can't say for certain that it's related to the upcoming event, but given the timing and location, I thought it might be worth mentioning.

If you've noticed anything unusual yourself, or have time to compare notes, I'd really appreciate the opportunity to discuss it further. You can reach me by calling this scientific report line at 468-663. I have already cleared your desk phone extension as a priority caller.

And, Frank, I'd suggest proceeding with caution. Events like this are rare, and they often leave questions that take time to unravel.
 Let me know if there's anything I can do to help.

(Phone voice) No more messages.

10/6/2026: edited by AH

(Phone voice) The person at extension 3... 1... 4... 1... 1... 2... (Melissa/Blair Paul). You have two messages.

Sunday, June 25, 1995 at 2:21 p.m.

Hi, Melissa. It's Arthur. Listen, I just wanted to touch base about the Holomax stuff.

I've been hearing some confusing chatter from Frank. He's saying things are moving fast, too fast maybe. He mentioned working with hardware that didn't pass final checks. And, well, you know me. I'm not trying to slow down the show right before the premiere this Friday. But when things start sounding risky, especially with something as new as this, I get twitchy.

I saw that question from Frank about bumping the premiere timeline. I wasn't looped in before that went out. And I'll be honest, it caught me off guard.

You know how important this relaunch is for us? If Holomax crashes on day one, it's not just a tech failure, it's a legacy problem.

Anyway, give me a call when you can. I am probably overreacting. I know how much Frank has been putting into this, but just, we can't stall again. We have talked about this too many times and made more public announcements than we probably should have to unveil the projector that will revolutionize film. But we only get one shot at a first impression.

Thank you for your hard work, Melissa. See you on Monday so we can discuss the premiere and check the books again before Blockbuster season is up.

(Voice) Last, message. Thursday, June 29, 195 at 10:56 a.m.

Melissa, Arthur here. I need you to call me. Now.

I just got off the phone with two different creditors. Two, not one.

They're saying we're months behind on payments for the concession contracts and the parts bought from a scrapyard now.

That's not a rounding error, Melissa. That's half a fiscal year. And what's worse, they somehow have my name listed as the backup signer on one of the accounts. That was never agreed to. Ever.

I dont know how this happened, but they're expecting me to answer for it. And now, I'm hearing Frank's not even on site.

He was supposed to walk me through the testing protocols this morning, and now no one's seen him since late last night.

I don't want to believe he skipped out the day before his invention is debuted. But if he did, and this whole thing backfires, that's on us.

This is spiraling, Melissa. Fast.

If you're sitting on something I don't know about, you have to tell me. We can't keep pretending it's under control if it's not. Call me back immediately.

(Phone voice) No more messages.

Sorry, but the user's mailbox can't accept more messages.

Yeah. You've reached the wrong person. Again.

I don't know what Atlas9 is. At this point, I don't care. I never worked there. I'm not involved. I'm not whoever you seem to think I am.

So, to whoever keeps calling, Agent 779, some sort of facade or whatever name you're using, please stop.

I don't owe you anything. I don't want to be involved. This is harassment now. Do not leave a message. Do not contact me again. And if you're listening, I hope you never find what this number goes to.

I wish I never had it attached to my name.

10/6/2026: edited by AH

Oh, are you the one who's been answering those e-mails? Oh, thank goodness, really. Thank you for calling. I didn't think I'd get a chance to explain all this.

I'm Melissa Hartwell, the manager over at Atlas9.

Now, I need you to understand - what happened the other night. It wasn't just some glitch or a bad show. The Holomax didn't just hiccup. It flat out overloaded on me. And yes, it was under my direction. I'll admit it.

I must not have followed every step Frank laid out for me. I panicked. I cut some corners. I thought I could keep it under control, but when Frank Uffin(?) disappeared that week, I didn't have time to figure it all out. I just winged it, like I thought he might have done.

Honestly, I almost called the whole premiere off when he didn't show, but it felt like it was on me to keep our theater alive.

So Friday, when I started to fire up the Holomax for the big Scavengers battle scene, the gauges just went dead.

I tore through Frank's notes, ran down to the power room hoping to restart things, but the machine looked normal. Pulsing steady(?).

Then when I reached for the levers to crank the power, my vision just went black.

When I came to, I was on the floor with my head pounding. I looked up at the clock and realized I'd missed my queue completely. The premier was already over.

I ran back into the auditorium and everything was wrong. The crowd I'd left just minutes before? Pure chaos. Projector cables hangin' loose, flailing out of their sockets. And the screen? Lord help me. The characters were coming out of it. Not projections. Real.

The Scavengers themselves - Fuzz(?) and Roy - right there in the room. It felt like a fever dream. I was terrified. Didn't know what to do. But the audience was so small and I couldn't bare to see 'em hurt.

I grabbed as many folks as I could and hid 'em in the projector sitting on my office desk. That was the only place I thought they'd be safe.

I was just about to barricade my office when I heard screeching tires and this huge crash out in the parking lot, like something had just arrived.

Then there was this hum. Not just a sound, but this low horrible vibration that shook me clear through.

I bolted out the back and the whole sky lit up electric blue. Not lightning. Not whether. Nothing I'd ever seen before. It was like the sky itself was coming down.

Serious. I swear to you I'm not crazy. I didn't run 'cause I was guilty. I ran 'cause I knew if I stayed, whatever that was would have erased me along with the place.

Look I know I messed up, but I didn't do this on purpose. I was trying to save our theater.

I don't think I'll be coming back to Atlas9 but please check on the folks in that projector. There's a red button on the side of it. Make sure they've got enough popcorn to hold them over before you look for the others still trapped inside the theater.

And be careful. I reckon FACADE is already on the hunt for 'em.

Man: Excuse me ma'am. You know anything about theater business? I have a few questions about your prior employer before you catch your flight...

Female: This call may be recorded. This voice path is secure.

Man (tape recorder sound): Agent, your subterfuge was insufficient. We observed your communication. The conspiracy theorist, the encrypted memos, your attempts to embed yourself among our ranks like a shadow. You were seen from the beginning. FACADE sees all.

You mistake your proximity to the agency name for protection. You're standing in a building wired with memory, sensors, and cameras. Yet you believed a clever, false report would cloak your intent? No. FACADE catalogs behavior, not words. And your behavior has drawn attention.

(tape recorder sound stops)

Listen, I shouldn't say this, but I did what I could to warn them.

Melissa, Arthur, and Frank. None of them listened.

And now, you're the one left to clean up the fractures they left behind.

The main case of FACADE's interest is Frank Roberts, the projection is an alleged missing person. Emphasis on alleged. He is not and was not ever missing.

He has somehow embedded himself within Starbot. In the barn scene specifically, he can even be glimpsed behind the door in the film, like he was caught on set where he shouldn't be.

It wasn't just his favorite movie moment. It was his escape hatch. You can even see him there now. The poster in his quarters is not some fan made self insert from a man in love with the movies. That is him.

He projected himself into it in some way. We do not know how. He is inside the film, and he is the only one who can bring the Holomax back online, back to its full power.

You must not let FACADE bring him back out of that poster. Who knows what they will use the Holomax for next if they can figure out how to control it? But that is all I can say for now. And I have already said too much.

(tape recorder sound start)

You are now under investigation for your attempted misguidance of the Prime Directive, and, as you well know, FACADE cannot proceed without Frank Roberts and the information he used to build the Holomax.

You will not maintain your status as an agent unless you act now, and seek to report every detail you can find about this man. Prove yourself still of use to this agency and find a way to bring the Holomax online. FACADE is watching.

You have your orders. Agent, you are now dismissed.

(Recording stops)
